chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Laythi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'and an abandoned well and a lofty palace'
He said: The Abandoned Well is the Silent Imam, and the Lofty Palace is the Speaking Imam.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'abandoned well' and 'lofty palace' in Surah Al-Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this allegorical interpretation of Surah Al-Hajj 22:45, distinguishing between the 'abandoned well' (Imam al-Samt), who holds divine knowledge in silence, and the 'lofty palace' (Imam al-Natiq), who actively disseminates it. This distinction highlights the dynamic nature of Imamate, where the presence of the Imam may be concealed or his voice muted during periods of political oppression, yet his spiritual authority remains intact.
